message.content: {"summary":"You present a clear, well-motivated reef-monitoring mission with explicit users and a strong Australian rationale, supported by a readable Gantt-based plan and a sensible STK software choice. Presentation is clean and professional. To progress, you need quantified mission requirements, a corrected orbit statement (600 km is LEO, not geostationary), fuller source details, contingency planning, and actual preliminary design results rather than tutorial completion alone.","next_steps":["Convert your user needs into quantified mission requirements (ground sample distance, revisit time, data latency, swath, design lifetime) and add an explicit objectives statement in the Mission Concept & Rationale section.","Correct the orbit claim in the Project Plan: 600 km is low Earth orbit and cannot be geostationary or provide continuous reef stare; revisit your end-of-life options to align with debris-mitigation practice.","Produce and interpret at least one preliminary technical result (e.g. an STK coverage/revisit or link-budget output) and resolve the Gantt/text editing-week inconsistency, adding contingency allowance and a planned-source list."],"criteria":{"C1":"You clearly explain the mission purpose, name the users (marine and conservation scientists, ground stations) and give a compelling Australian rationale with referencing. To reach the top of Accomplished, add quantified requirements (resolution, revisit, latency, lifetime) and an explicit objectives statement. Also correct the 2017 coral-loss claim and reframe '30 percent more acidic' as a pH change (~0.1 unit).","C2":"Your Gantt chart has weekly columns, task rows, deadlines and descriptions, and the sequence is feasible and tied to launch, orbit, ground, comms and end-of-life. The next level requires contingency provision, a planned information-source list linked to tasks, and fixing the inconsistency where your text schedules editing in weeks 7–8 but the chart shows weeks 9–10.","C3":"Your reported progress is background reading and completion of STK tutorials 1–4. To move beyond Adequate, present actual preliminary design results, calculations or simulation output with brief interpretation. Note that the orbit claim as written (600 km geostationary) is incorrect, so it cannot yet count as evidence of useful design work.","C4":"Your report is logically structured with clear headings, readable professional prose, consistent formatting and a labelled, explained Gantt figure; superscript citations match your numbered source list. To reach the top of Accomplished, replace bare URLs with full references (author, title, date, source) in a consistent standard format and ensure every in-text citation matches."}}
message.reasoning:
We need to produce JSON with summary (<=80 words), next_steps (3 strings), criteria object with C1-C4 each <=70 words.

Must be formative, address student as "you", cite sections/figures, name what they did well, state what next rubric level requires. Don't change marks. Don't comment on conversion artefacts. Don't make up explanations.

Let's craft.

Summary <=80 words: acknowledge strengths: clear reef-monitoring rationale with users, Gantt plan, STK choice, clean presentation. Then gaps: unquantified requirements, orbit error (600 km vs GEO), informal sources, limited technical evidence.

Next steps: 3 actionable items.

C1: 8/10 Accomplished — praise mission purpose, users, Australian rationale, referencing; next level requires quantified requirements (GSD, revisit, latency, swath, lifetime) and explicit objectives; fix coral statistic and acidification phrasing.

C2: 6/10 Adequate — Gantt with weekly tasks, deadlines, feasible sequence; next level requires contingency provisions, planned information sources linked to tasks, and resolving the weeks 7–8 vs 9–10 editing inconsistency.

C3: 4/10 Adequate — background reading and four STK tutorials; next level requires actual preliminary design results/calculations/simulation output; correct the orbit claim (600 km is LEO, not GEO) so it can count as evidence.

C4: 7/10 Accomplished — clear headings, readable prose, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt figure, superscript citations matching list; next level requires full reference details (author, title, date) in a standard format.

Keep each <=70 words. Count roughly.

Write JSON only.
